editorial:
Imagine having a dad who is literally out of this world. You get to follow Lera, a 15-year-old girl in Vladivostok who barely knows her father because he lives on the Mira space station. He is basically just a voice on the phone to her. The vibe starts off as a sad family story, but everything changes when a meteor shower hits the city. Suddenly, it turns into a high-stakes race against time. You feel the tension as Lera has to navigate a collapsing city while her dad watches her every move from space, guiding her through the chaos using satellites. It is a cool mix of a family drama and a disaster movie that keeps you wondering if they will ever actually hug.

What really works here is the bond between the father and daughter. The acting feels real, and the action scenes are exciting without being too confusing. While some of the slow parts in the middle might make you want to check your phone, the payoff is worth it. If you love movies about space and family, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, Lera manages to stop the disaster by following her father's precise instructions from the station. The big twist is the emotional realization that their connection was stronger than the distance. After the city is saved, the movie wraps up with a heartfelt reunion. Her father finally returns to Earth, and Lera gets the parent she has missed for years, proving that love can bridge the gap between space and home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family stories and sci-fi disasters.
